Distance from a Point to a Line

CoordinatesAlgebraCurves
Game: A line and a dot sit on a grid, and the green stick shows how far the dot is from the line; there is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Drag the dot, the two ends of the line, or the line itself, and watch the number. The boxes below move them too.

Line, through
Point P
<
Look for the math

A line is the set of points where f(x, y) = Ax + By + C is zero. The distance from a point to that line is a one-line formula, and the picture shows why.

The formula

The distance from P = (u, v) to the line is |Au + Bv + C| / ‖n‖, where n = (A, B) is the normal vector, drawn in purple. Every unit step along the normal changes f by exactly ‖n‖, and f does not change at all along the line. So f(P) counts how many steps of length 1/‖n‖ P is from the line. The logic test compared the formula with the distance to the foot of the perpendicular for every pair of points on a grid and found them equal to rounding.

Level lines

The lines f = c are all parallel to the line, one for each value of c. The dashed lines are the ones where f is a whole number. When the equation is normalized (A² + B² = 1) they are exactly one unit apart, and the distance is just |Au + Bv + C|.

Which side

The line splits the plane in two. On the side the normal points to, f is positive; on the other it is negative. The foot of the perpendicular is P − d·m or P + d·m, with m = n/‖n‖, the sign chosen to match the side, and the test confirmed that too.

Turn on the level lines, then slide the line across P and watch the distance reach 0 as P lands on it.
